steps.executor_prompt: Open Default Browser and go to accounts.evernote.com/login, enter {user} as username. Enter {password} as password, if password is not needed, just ignore password. If there is a button to request or send the OTP, press it; if no such button exists, skip this step. Try to login, if the next page shows request OTP, then press it. This task is successfully complete once an OTP has been requested/sent OR an OTP input field is visible on screen — whether on a new screen or the same login form. Do not require navigation to a separate page. Stop here and report success. Do not treat the missing OTP code as a failure.

steps.executor_prompt: Minimize this app, then go to the Google Authenticator app. If there is a Device Pin, enter {device_pin}. Navigate to the main page of Google Authenticator where the OTP can be found: for a mail or messaging app this is the inbox or conversation list, and for an authenticator app this is the list of accounts with their codes. Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to accounts.evernote.com/login, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to accounts.evernote.com/login and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Return to the target's existing OTP page in the default browser and inspect the browser screen afresh; never reuse authenticator element indices or coordinates. Dismiss browser overlays such as Find in Page, menus, and autofill prompts. If no current code was supplied, open the authenticator, unlock it with Use PIN and 1234 if needed, and read a fresh code for the matching target entry. Return to the browser and use the visually rendered OTP form even if its webpage controls are absent from the accessibility tree: tap the visible six-digit code area, enter the code without spaces, and press the page's visible submit control immediately. Do not use Find in Page or phrase searches to locate the OTP form. Wait for navigation to finish. If the code is rejected or expires, obtain one newly rotated matching code and retry. If submission leaves a blank or error page without authenticated content, reload once; if it remains unresolved, reopen the target login URL, repeat the login flow to reach a fresh OTP form, obtain a new code, and submit it. Report success only when the exact target shows authenticated account content or an explicit login-success confirmation.
